items.title: fix(pm-aggregator): kill the residual first-pass latency tail (#5082)
items.body: Follow-up to #9585 (which fixed /program size and /quota latency). The pool-quota steward's step-6 watch caught a residual latency tail on two consecutive runs (367: / 16.86s, /today 8.97s pass 1; 368: / 17.5s, /today 9.7s pass 1; pass 2 clean both times). ## Root cause (measured live) 1. **The activity scan blocked the event loop for ~15.5s.** `buildQuotaAnalytics`'s activity computation ran as one synchronous `setTimeout` block of `json_each` scans over `session_message` — measured per query: tool rows 7.38s, skill rows 3.81s, shell rows 4.00s. It re-runs every 10 min, triggered by any /quota or /api/quota-analytics.json read. Every request queued behind it — reproduced: a polling `/` request stalled **13.58s** concurrent with one trigger, and the `/` shell handler has no awaits of its own, so it cannot be slow any other way. 2. **Blocking-expiry page caches.** Board/overview/today contexts sat behind a 10s TTL cache where the first request after expiry paid the full cold assembly (measured /board cold 8.2s, /frag/overview cold 2.7-4.0s). 3. The aggregates SWR refresh chunked per query, but the widest single scans still blocked ~2.6s each (leg rows 15d 2.65s, day-of-week full history 2.56s). ## Fix - Activity computation: 12h slices, one query per macrotask (~0.1-0.5s widest slice), merged by summation — totals are exactly the whole-window counts. - Aggregates refresh: all wide scans sliced (day slices for the 15d/7d/21d windows, 30d chunks for day-of-week history from the coverage read); cold-path queries keep their exact original unbounded semantics. - `TodayCache` is now stale-while-revalidate: expired entries serve stale immediately, one single-flight background refresh re-reads; cold loads still coalesce, failures never poison, `clear()` still forces a fresh read (generation guard). Contract tests updated to the SWR semantics + a failed-refresh-keeps-stale test. - Boot warm-up also warms board/overview/today contexts. ## Verification - Old vs new `buildQuotaAnalytics` against the live DB (cold + refreshed outputs): match within live-traffic drift and window-anchor effects; only structural delta is tie order in activity `topSkills`. - Cache contract: all unit assertions pass (standalone runner + updated test files; the repo test files' server-boot sections time out identically on unmodified main in this laptop environment — fixture boot takes ~12s under current load — so CI is the arbiter there). - `tsc --noEmit`: no errors in touched files; total error count identical pre/post (pre-existing unrelated test-file errors). - Live before/after timings incl. cold passes after TTL expiry: posted on #5082 after deploy. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Performance** * Large analytics scans are processed in smaller time-based batches, reducing the work performed in any single step. * Startup now warms additional dashboard and overview data. * **Bug Fixes** * Expired Today data is served immediately while a background refresh runs, avoiding delays on cache expiry. * If a refresh fails, the previous data remains available and a later request can retry.

items.title: fix(pm-aggregator): /program compact pool rows + /quota analytics aggregates cache (#5082)
items.body: Fixes both live defects tracked on #5082 (PM broker surfaces), measured by the pool-quota steward on 2026-11-13. ## 1. /program HTML regrowth — 4,077,305 B and climbing daily **Root cause (measured, not guessed).** The pool section rendered every one of the 1,422 Project #4 pool items as a full interactive card (~2,791 B median): title/badges/links ~0.65 KB + status-request actbox **1,702,156 B total** + derived brief panel **1,347,229 B total**. The pool only ever grows — the orchestrator adds every filed item and nothing ever leaves — and 725 of the 1,422 items are Done. Daily growth tracked the filing rate (~+24 KB/day at plateau, +140–190 KB on busy days). /api/program.json stayed 26 KB the whole time: the growth was all HTML card furniture, none of it data. A Done item's brief is formulaic ("Next: No action — this item is done") and its actbox is an action control for work that is finished. **Fix (render.ts, `projectsBodyHtml`).** Full cards now render only for active work (Project status In Progress / In Review) and for epics at any status — an epic's rollup/forecast/spend are its substance (#3984, #4824) and epics are few (40). Every other item renders as a compact row — title, status/area/horizon/kind/state badges, issue + Project-item links, updated date — the same compact shape the per-project pages already use. The ⚠ disagreement badge still renders on compact rows, so no signal is lost. Counts, area chips, weights, the area filter and saved views all operate on the whole pool exactly as before; the JSON twins are untouched. Pool-section body, same live pool, old vs new code: **4,112,551 B → 1,067,703 B**. Full cards for active items are byte-identical to before (verified modulo the per-render form token). Page growth is now bounded by the active pool, not by cumulative history. **Tradeoff, stated plainly:** a Todo/Done non-epic item no longer carries its brief panel or status-request form on /program (both remain on its full surfaces — board/item views and GitHub). One test fixture follows the new contract: the #1279 forwarded-brief test in curation-1497.test.ts now uses an In Progress fixture, since briefs render on full cards; its with/without forwarding assertions are unchanged. ## 2. /quota slow — 5–19 s per load **Root cause (measured in-process against the live 21.7 GB OpenCode ledger, 656k route_attempt rows).** `buildQuotaAnalytics` ran seven route_attempt aggregate scans per build; only the two burn scans were cached (120 s). The other five — last-hour burn, credential coverage, hourly-7d, **day-of-week over the entire table (no WHERE)**, daily-21d — ran on **every** request: ~5.4 s of scans per warm build, ~10 s cold, all synchronous on Bun's single event loop, so concurrent page loads queued behind each other's scans (hence /quota at 9.4 s / 18.8 s and knock-on stalls on / and /today). Baseline in-process: cold 9,309 ms, warm ~5,100 ms. /api/quota.json was always fast (0.04 s) because it never builds analytics. **Fix (analytics-store.ts + server.ts).** All route_attempt aggregates now ride ONE stale-while-revalidate cache (5 min TTL, the loadActivity pattern this codebase already uses for its other slow scan): a fresh copy is served directly; a stale copy is served immediately while a background refresh recomputes one query per macrotask, so a refresh never monopolizes the loop. The first build in a process computes synchronously, and server.ts now pays that once at boot with a warm-up call, off the request path. The SQL is byte-for-byte the same queries, regrouped behind query helpers. **Equivalence:** old vs new builder output on identical inputs differs only by 4 route attempts that landed in the ~50 s between the two runs (attemptsTo and the counts containing them); every projection, window, unlock picture and WoW delta is identical. Warm build: **~5,100 ms → ~2 ms**; a stale-read build returns in ~2 ms with the previous aggregates. ## Verification (laptop, worktree) - `bunx tsc --noEmit`: error set identical to pristine main (zero new; none in src/). - `bun test` (full aggregator suite, 192 files): named-failure set identical to the pristine-main baseline (the live-source #1138/#1139/#1140 trio, the #1195 boot test, and load-sensitive hook timeouts fail on main too). The four suites covering pool cards (epics, forecast #3984, spend #4824, curation #1497) pass 35/35. - Live before/after numbers are posted on #5082 after deploy. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Project pool items that aren’t in progress or review, and aren’t epics, now appear as compact cards with key status and issue details. Active work and epics retain their full cards. * **Improvements** * Analytics views can reuse recent results and continue showing cached data while updates refresh. * Quota analytics now load at startup when possible, with a later retry if loading fails.

items.title: fix(aggregator): TTL-cache + single-flight the board/overview/program assemblies (#5082)
items.body: ## What this fixes The remaining layer of #5082. The payload-bounding half landed in #7753 and the projector outage underneath is repaired, but the board-family assembly itself was still re-run live on **every** request: `boardContext()` / `overviewContext()` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts` fan out to a Kaneo login + poll (sequential per-project task pagination), one projector `/links` call per board card, and the `items()` closure — with no TTL cache and no coalescing. Under ordinary fleet load that assembly outlives the 10 s dashboard deadline (`assembly-deadline.ts`), so `/board`, `/api/board.json`, `/api/overview.json`, and `/program` 503 even with every upstream healthy (verified live 2026-11-10: all four 503 at ~10.1–10.5 s while a single projector `/links` took 0.05 s and `/api/quota.json` answered in ~1.4 s). Concurrent cold loads each started their own assembly (measured 2026-11-08: 3 concurrent → 3 assemblies, all 503). ## Design The assemblies get the exact contract `/today` already has (#1179), reusing its class unchanged (`src/today-cache.ts`): - `loadBoardContext()` (was `boardContext()`) now runs through a `TodayCache` — **TTL 10 s** (`TODAY_CACHE_TTL_MS`, inside #1179's accepted 5–15 s window and 6× tighter than the 60 s health-probe cache) — and `boardContext()` is the cached accessor. Every existing caller benefits: `/board`, `/api/board.json`, the overview, `/today`, the queue, provenance priming. - `loadOverviewContext()` gets the same wrap (`overviewContext()`), covering `/`, `/frag/overview`, `/api/overview.json`. Its board leg rides the board cache, so a cold overview and a cold board share one board assembly. - The `/program` + `/api/program.json` handler's live-source fan-out is extracted to `loadProgramSources()` behind the same cache (`programSources()`); the local-store reads (`commentFormOpts`, `actionsStore.byObject()`) and everything view-dependent stay per-request. Single-flight: concurrent cold requests share one in-flight load (`TodayCache` coalescing). A throwing load is never cached — the slot releases and the next request retries, so the error boundary behaves exactly as before. Fail-soft facet fallbacks (e.g. an empty board when Kaneo is down) are cached as-is until expiry: they are the honest degraded state of that read, the same truthfulness rule #1179 documents. Provenance (`prov()` / `provDetail()`) is still read live per request at the call sites, never from the cache. The existing deadline + stale-fallback layer (`assembly-deadline.ts`: 10 s deadline, last-good up to 5 min, 2 MB cap, keyed by pathname+search) is **unchanged** — it is now the second line of defense instead of the only one, and warm hits return in milliseconds so it should rarely engage. One stacking note: `/today`'s board leg can now lag up to ~20 s worst case (its own 10 s cache over the board cache's 10 s). Both bounds were accepted independently for this class of display data; noted here so it's a decision, not an accident. ## Variant inventory (why no cache keys are needed) The caches sit **below** the variant split — they hold the variant-free assembly, and every variant is derived per request from it — so a variant body can never be served for another variant, by construction: | Route | Variants found | Where the split happens | |---|---|---| | `/board` | `?done=all`; saved views (`vf.*`, `view`, `viewer`) | `renderBoard` / view filter in the handler, from the shared context | | `/api/board.json` | `?done=all` (#7753); saved views (#8058) | `boardJsonBody` / `boardJsonViewBody` per request | | `/api/overview.json` | none | `deriveOverview` per request | | `/frag/overview` | none | `deriveOverview` + render per request | | `/program`, `/api/program.json` | saved views (pool filtering); `?area=` (render-only) | handler derivations from the cached source bundle | Deliberately left uncached: `boardRender`'s per-request local-store reads (actions/comments counts, comment form options) and `/program`'s briefs/forecasts — cheap local reads where freshness matters more. `/api/program.json` is not in `BOUNDED_DASHBOARD_PATHS` today (pre-existing); it shares the now-cached handler assembly but its deadline behavior is unchanged. The `/attention` page's own `attentionContext` path is untouched (it is cached only as part of the overview assembly). ## Deploy path Aggregator source + tests only; no `pkgs/` or Nix module changes. Deployment is **merge → `nixos-rebuild switch`**: the packaged aggregator from the pm-stack packaging change (`pkgs/pm-aggregator`, `fix/8171-pm-stack-nix-apps`) picks this up from the store — not a checkout pull. ## Test evidence New tests in `test/board-cache-5082.test.ts` (9 tests): - (a) concurrent cold loads coalesce to one underlying assembly (gated loader, 3 waiters, loader called once); - (b) a second request inside the TTL does not re-run the assembly (fake clock, same object); - (c) at TTL expiry the assembly reloads; - (d) a failed assembly is never cached — next request retries and its success caches; - (e) `?done=all` vs the default body: both derived from a single shared assembly (loader called once, identical context object), default done strip = 100 (`DONE_STRIP_RENDER_LIMIT`), `?done=all` = all 150, each body shipping exactly its visible cards' items; - route wiring through a booted fixture-mode server: warm `/api/board.json` byte-identical, `?done=all` never cross-serves after the default ran, 5 concurrent requests serve one body, `/board` + `/board?done=all` render, `/api/overview.json` warm byte-identical, `/frag/overview` renders, `/program` + `/api/program.json` serve. Counts (laptop, worktree, `PM_AGG_FRESHNESS_PORT` moved off 4871): - Required set — `board-cache-5082` + `board-json-5082` + `board-json-view-8058` + `boot`: **35 pass / 0 fail** (196 expect() calls). - Post-merge re-run including `today-cache-1179` + `assembly-deadline`: **60 pass / 0 fail** (309 expect() calls). - `tsc --noEmit`: **0 errors in `src/`** and 0 in the new test file (pre-existing `test/` errors on main untouched). - Full aggregator suite: 2160 pass / 9 fail — and the **same 9 fail on pristine `origin/main`** (verified by stashing this change and re-running those 7 files: 191 pass / 9 fail). Pre-existing, unrelated (live-source registry, epic ETA, collector parsing, dns page, pool assembly). - Boot smoke (fixture mode, alternate ports): `/board` cold 21 ms → warm 2–6 ms; `/api/overview.json` cold 10 ms → warm 1 ms. Fixture assemblies are cheap, so treat this as directional — the production effect is skipping a multi-second live assembly per request, which is what the unit tests pin. Fixes #5082 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(pm-aggregator): slice day-of-week history in 2-day chunks (#5082)
items.body: Follow-up to #9589. Its post-deploy probe (1,142 polls of `/` over 6.2 min across the activity recompute boundary, analytics triggered every 20s) found ONE remaining 3.25s stall. Cause: day-of-week history chunks were 30 days; with ~20 days of history that is the whole unbounded scan in a single step — measured 2.58s. This slices it in 2-day chunks (~0.3s each, merged by summation, output unchanged). Everything else in the probe: max ≤0.5s. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(aggregator): restore pm-stack suite on main — table captions/scopes, active pool fixture, Playwright spec out of bun test (#10469)
items.body: Fixes #10469 — pm-stack tests run 43696785135 on main (9ce1dbfb98) failed with 4 aggregator failures. Three distinct root causes: 1. **Table semantics (#1215)** — `queuePanelHtml` in `src/render.ts` (queue panel, landed 2026-11-14 in be5d6c5740) added two tables with no `` and 13 header cells with no `scope`. Both tables now open with a caption and every header cell carries `scope="col"`, matching the rest of render.ts. 2. **Pool card status-request test** — the #5082 compact-row change deliberately renders only active work (In Progress / In Review) and epics as full cards with the status-request form; other statuses render compact with action badges only. The #1154/#1156 test fixture was still a `Todo` item, so the form it asserts never rendered. The fixture is now an active (`In Progress`) item, with a comment naming the #5082 rule; all five assertions are unchanged, and the pending-request badge still renders on compact rows exactly as #5082 intended. 3. **Playwright spec under `bun test`** — `bun test` was loading `test/browser/mobile-work-view.spec.ts`, a Playwright acceptance spec, which registers Playwright hooks outside a Playwright run and fails. New `bunfig.toml` (`[test] pathIgnorePatterns`) excludes `test/browser/**` from bun test; the spec still runs under its own runner (pm-aggregator-tests browser job via `playwright.config.ts`). Verification (laptop worktree from 9ce1dbfb98, fixture env `PM_AGG_SOURCE=fixtures PM_AGG_DEV=1`): - `bun test test/a11y-1215.test.ts` — 14 pass, 0 fail. - Pool-card test (`bun test test/actions.test.ts -t 'pool card carries the request control'`) — pass, 5 expect() calls. - `bunx playwright test --config playwright.config.ts --grep pmo_mob_03/04` — 1 passed. - Full `bun test` — 2715 pass / 22 fail across 210 files (was 211; the spec is no longer double-run). The 22 remaining failures are pre-existing laptop-environment failures (server-boot tests collide with the live pm-aggregator service's ports; live-source tests need the live feed): `test/boot.test.ts` produces the identical 14 failures on clean main and with this change applied. - `bunx tsc --noEmit` — clean. Queue: task 17355, lane any-a. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(pm-aggregator): take the registry merge off the /program + /board request path (#5082)
items.body: ## The recurrence Pool-quota-steward run 381 (2026-11-14 09:20Z), after #9596 and #9835 were deployed and verified: `/api/program.json` **503 at 10.51 s**, `/program` **503 at 10.41 s**, `/board` 200 at 10.53 s — every other surface fast, pass 2 all fast. The aggregator had not restarted (up since the 02:02 CST deploy, `NRestarts=0`), ruling out the boot-stall family. **Reproduced live** the same morning with a timestamped probe loop: one cycle measured `/api/program.json` 10.52 s, `/program` 10.56 s, `/board` 6.18 s while `/today` (0.04 s), `/quota` (0.13 s) and a direct projector `/comments` read (0.001 s) stayed fast — then all fast again once one slow attempt completed. ## Root cause `commentFormOpts()` is awaited on the request path of all three routes, and its identities half ran `source.registry()` **uncached, every request**. `registry()` merges the feed with a live map of the laptop OpenCode server; `mapServerSessions` walks 3 + up to 120 **sequential** fetches with 10 s aborts. Healthy, the map costs ~0.5 s (measured). When the server stalls under load, one map costs 6–10.5 s — and because only successes were cached (45 s), a failed map was re-paid in full by the next assembly. Three sequential steward probes each paid it; the two program routes' last-good was older than the 30-minute stale cap, so the deadline fallback was a hard 503. ## Fix - `server.ts`: the identities half of `commentFormOpts` rides a `TodayCache` stale-while-revalidate (the same contract as the page assemblies), warmed at boot with them. The per-request `githubRefs` half is never cached. After the first load, no request on these routes ever waits on the registry merge. - `sources/live.ts`: `laptopMapped` shares one in-flight map between concurrent callers and remembers a failed map for 15 s (the two legs are extracted unchanged into `mapLaptopServers`). Remaining `registry()` consumers (search, discuss, the registry page) stop re-paying a stall per call; a null map already reads as "unreachable on the last read" to the coverage facet, so the brief negative window changes no one's story. ## Tests - New `test/laptop-map-cache-5082.test.ts` (3 tests): failed map remembered (stub hit count flat across repeat `registry()` calls), concurrent callers share one in-flight map (1 fetch for 5 callers), successful map still cached 45 s. The first two **fail on the unpatched code** (verified), the third pins the existing contract. - Neighbouring suites (`today-cache`, `latest-comments`, `board-cache`, `program-prime`, `assembly-deadline`, `opencode`, `program`, `registry-ref-filter`, `supabase-export`): 74 pass / 3 fail on this branch — the identical 3 failures occur on base (booted-server hook timeouts from the laptop's live-service port collision, the known flake). - `tsc --noEmit`: no errors in touched files (the one environment-level `bun` types error is identical on base). Refs #5082 (evidence comment with post-deploy probe numbers follows there). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Performance** * Cached author identity information is reused across comment-form requests, reducing repeated registry lookups. * Concurrent requests for laptop session mappings now share the same lookup. Successful mappings are reused, and failed lookups are briefly cached to avoid repeated server requests. * **Tests** * Added coverage for failed and concurrent lookups, and for reusing successful mappings.

items.title: fix(pm-aggregator): freshness invalidation serves stale instead of paying the cold overview assembly (#5082)
items.body: ## What Fixes the /api/overview.json cold first-pass 503 (and the slow cold first passes on the sibling bounded routes) in the #5082 family. ## Root cause (measured) 1. **Freshness notices drop the overview assembly entirely.** `freshnessStore.onNotice` called `overviewContextCache.clear()` / `todayContextCache.clear()`, and `TodayCache.clear()` nulls the cached value. Notices land every few minutes — 115 in the 3 h before steward run 379; journal entries at 06:17:26Z and 07:17:20Z sit seconds before steward runs 378/379 started. 2. **The first post-notice request pays the full cold assembly on the request path.** With the value dropped, `TodayCache.get()` takes the cold-miss branch and awaits `loadOverviewContext` (attention + projects + quota + health + board + orchestration fan-out). Measured post-notice first passes tonight: 0.65–1.01 s in mild conditions (5 notice-triggered probe samples), but the chain's cost is condition-dependent and unbounded — the same class of chain measured 17.83 s (#9596-era /api/program.json) and 26.4 s post-restart. 3. **The deadline fallback can't save an hourly reader.** `/api/overview.json` is deadline-bounded at 10 s with a last-good fallback capped at 5 minutes' staleness. An hourly watch's last good is ~1 h old, so when the chain inflated past 10 s under load (steward 378: 503; steward 379: 503 at 10.42 s / 112 B, with /board 10.65 s and /program 6.05 s in the same pass), the answer was a hard 503. Pass 2 was always clean because pass 1's shared run seeded both caches. Ruled out live: the projector reconcile is NOT on the overview cold path — during a window where a direct projector `/comments` read took 19.4 s, a post-notice /api/overview.json first pass still measured 0.65 s. The sibling slowness in run 379 is the same first-pass-after-idle pattern on their own per-request legs, which the wider staleness cap below now covers with a marked-stale serve instead of a stall-or-503. ## Fix - **`TodayCache.invalidate()`** (new): marks the entry expired but keeps it servable. The next `get()` takes the ordinary stale-while-revalidate branch — serve the retained assembly immediately, refresh behind it. `clear()` is unchanged. - **`server.ts` onNotice**: invalidate (not clear) the overview/today assemblies, and kick both background refreshes at notice time. #3976's intent is preserved — an accepted revision becomes visible one assembly later — but no request ever pays the rebuild. - **`assembly-deadline.ts`**: `MAX_STALE_AGE_MS` 5 min → 30 min, with the reasoning inline. Stale responses are explicitly marked (`x-aggregator-stale`; `stale`/`staleReason` in JSON), so the wider cap stays honest; anything older still 503s. Payload shape is untouched: `deriveOverview` and the route handlers are unchanged, so a normal (non-stale) response is byte-for-byte the same computation as before. ## Verification - 3 new `invalidate()` tests in `test/today-cache-1179.test.ts`; semantics also verified locally with a standalone harness (incl. the exact server.ts kick pattern: post-invalidate `get()` resolves with the retained value while the refresh is still blocked, fresh value lands after). - `test/assembly-deadline.test.ts`: all pass locally. - Pre-existing laptop states, identical before/after this change: `today-cache-1179.test.ts`'s booted-server hook times out on the laptop (port collision with the running service — CI runs it clean), and `tsc --noEmit` reports the same 22 errors in unrelated test fixtures on base and on this branch. Zero new errors in the touched files. - Post-deploy live acceptance (notice-triggered cold cycles + concurrent burst + payload equivalence) will be reported on #5082 after merge. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(aggregator): bound /api/board.json to the board the page shows (#5082)
items.body: ## What `/api/board.json` — the machine twin of `/board` — now returns **the board the page shows**, not the whole completion log. ## Why (root cause, named) The endpoint built its payload from `boardContext()` with no done policy and no strip limit: - **1 720 cards**, of which 1 483 were `done` (the full 7-day window) while `renderBoardBody` renders at most `DONE_STRIP_RENDER_LIMIT` (100) newest done cards. - **2 903 linked items** — the closure of every ref *every* card had ever linked. 2 546 of those items were reachable only through done cards, and only 337 cards were actually rendered. - Total: **2 717 429 B** measured on the live laptop aggregator (`127.0.0.1:4870`). That payload is past the aggregator's own **2 MB `MAX_CACHED_RESPONSE_BYTES`** (`src/assembly-deadline.ts`), so the 503/timeout path could never serve it as a stale response — and every request re-read the entire item closure, which is the shared assembly the steward's `000`/empty-reply observations trace to. ## Change - New `src/board-json.ts` (`boardJsonBody`): applies `applyBoardDonePolicy` (7-day done age-out + retired ROADMAP Done-table class) and the shared done-strip limit, then ships **only the items the visible cards link to**. Each card already carries its own `links`, so `items` is a resolution lookup, not a dump. - New `selectVisibleDoneCards` in `board-policy.ts`: the newest-N done selection, shared by `renderBoardBody` and the JSON twin so the two can never disagree again. - `/api/board.json` view branch filters the **already-bounded** board and keeps only those cards' items (no reintroduction of the closure). - Compact JSON for this endpoint (`jsonCompact`) — no 2-space padding for a machine consumer. - `?done=all` restores the full done strip, mirroring `/board?done=all`. Measured shape: **2 717 429 B → ~439 KB** on the same data (83.4% smaller, comfortably under the 2 MB cache limit). ## Tests - New `test/board-json-5082.test.ts` (6 cases): live-only items, 7-day age-out, retired Done-table class, newest-first strip cap, `?done=all`, custom limit, and bounded output under a 2 400-card completion log (>10× smaller than the unbounded form). - `test/boot.test.ts`: every shipped item resolves a link a shipped card carries; response is not pretty-printed. - `bun test` (targeted aggregates): **73 pass**. `bunx tsc --noEmit`: no `src/` errors (the two `test/` errors are pre-existing on `origin/main`). ## Notes / not in scope - This bounds the payload and the per-request item closure; it does not re-architect the facet assembly (explicitly out of scope in the packet). The `/program` HTML size concern is a separate symptom already split out under #5082's history. Fixes #5082 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(pm-aggregator): prime analytics cache sliced at boot, warm program assembly + briefs comments, SWR-cache latest-comments fan-out, bound /api/program.json (#9594, #9781)
items.body: ## What Fixes #9594 — the first `/program` / `/api/program.json` hit after an aggregator restart stalls for tens of seconds (26.44s / 26.48s on two controlled restarts; pool-quota-steward run 369 caught the same shape in the wild at 17.83s). Follow-up to the #5082 latency work (#9585/#9589/#9591, all merged today); #5082 itself stays closed — this is a distinct mechanism, tracked on #9594 and cross-linked there. ## Root cause (measured, not inferred) - The program legs are fast in a clean process: items 0.02s, projects 0.01s, roadmap 0.29s, orchestration 0.02s, coverageCensus 0.03s (programRefs = 8). Warm TTL-expiry first pass: 0.023s — the #9589 SWR cache works; expiry is not the stall. - The first `buildQuotaAnalytics` is fully synchronous: **12.23s** in a clean process (second build 0.00s). The boot warm-up ran it plus three cold context assemblies on the single Bun event loop; a 150ms poll through a restart shows exactly one 26.48s response — the first on the new process — then 0.03–0.06s throughout. Requests arriving during warm-up queue behind the whole window. - `programSources` was the one major assembly the warm-up omitted, so /program's first post-restart request always paid its cold fan-out on the request path, inside that backlog. With deploys restarting the service repeatedly (three today), first-pass-after-restart is the recurring shape. ## Change - `analytics-store.ts`: new `primeAttemptAggregates()` fills the aggregates cache through the existing day-sliced SWR refresh (widest slice ~0.3s, one per macrotask); `refreshAttemptAggregates` gains an `onSettled` callback so the prime is observable. - `server.ts`: the boot warm-up primes instead of building synchronously, and warms `programSources()` alongside board/overview/today. - Request-path semantics unchanged: a `/quota` request landing before the prime settles still pays the synchronous cold build on its own path, exactly as today. ## Tests - New `test/program-prime-5082.test.ts`: prime contract against a fixture `route_attempt` DB (prime starts once, in-flight/again primes are no-ops, missing DB fail-soft, primed coverage served by the build) + a booted fixture server serving `/api/program.json`. - Local run: the new file passes 3/3; neighboring #5082 suites (board-cache, today-cache, board-json) pass 15/16 — the one failure is a laptop-only EADDRINUSE on the freshness IPC port 4871 held by the live service, unrelated to this change. Typecheck shows 22 pre-existing errors in unrelated test files, none in the touched files. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Performance** * Analytics and program data are prepared during service startup, helping make the first requests for this information available without waiting for an on-demand refresh. When cached aggregate data is already current or unavailable, startup continues without starting a redundant refresh. ## Added 2026-11-13 (resumed lane): the projector-slow comments cliff — fixes #9781 The lane resumed after the sandbox↔laptop transport outage and found steward runs 376/377 had escalated the family from slow to failing: `/program` **503 on pass 1 in both runs** (11.38s / 11.57s), `/board` ~10s in the same passes. That shape is a second, distinct mechanism from the boot stall above, tracked on #9781: - Reproduced live with a timed probe loop: `/board` and `/program` — and only those two — took **8.11–8.55s per hit** for a ~3-minute window while `/api/program.json` held 0.04s. They are exactly the surfaces whose handlers call `briefCommentsFor` on every request. - `projectorLatestComments` fans out one projector `/comments` read per ref, every fetch under the getJson 8s abort, **uncached**. During the projector's 15-minute `/reconcile` sweep (run inline in the projector process; a direct `/comments` hit inside the window measured **11.2s** vs 0.0006s warm), each batch resolves at the 8s abort — the page pays ~8.2s, and past `/program`'s 10s assembly deadline (hourly last-good always older than the 5-minute stale window) it becomes the hard 503. Change (commit 0f99186): - `sources/live.ts`: `LatestCommentsCache` — per-ref stale-while-revalidate (60s TTL) in front of `projectorLatestComments`. Expired entries serve stale and refresh single-flight in the background; only never-seen refs read on the request path; failures never poison the cache (failed refresh keeps stale; failed cold read keeps the fixtures fallback for those refs, uncached). - `server.ts`: the boot warm-up also primes the briefs comments for the program pool refs (board briefs read a subset of the same refs). - `assembly-deadline.ts`: `/api/program.json` joins `BOUNDED_DASHBOARD_PATHS` — run 369's unbounded 17.83s becomes stale-or-503 at the deadline like its HTML twin. Tests: new `test/latest-comments-9781.test.ts` (4/4 pass) pins the cache contract; `test/assembly-deadline.test.ts` updated for the six-route set (all pass); touched files typecheck clean. The server-booting suites show the same laptop-only hook-timeout/EADDRINUSE flake against the live service noted above, on the base commit as well — not a regression.

items.title: feat(pm-stack): read route analytics from the OpenCode rollup API, not opencode.db
items.body: Refs developing-today-forks/opencode#2795 (slice 2, queue task 23389). Needs developing-today-forks/opencode#2831 merged and running on the laptop server first. Before: the /quota "Analytics & projection" section opened `opencode.db` read-only and ran its own SQL over `route_attempt` (legs by day, provider and credential; models by day and variant; last hour; hourly and daily totals; day-of-week history; coverage; credential coverage). After: every one of those reads goes to the OpenCode server's `GET /api/route/attempts/rollup`. Credentials arrive only as the server's `credentialKey` digest, and pool attribution hashes the ids from `quota-current.json` the same way to match, so the credential join still works without the id ever leaving the server. The section shows "unavailable" until the first refresh lands, instead of a synchronous cold build. How: new `src/route-rollup.ts` (client, `credentialKey`, `readRouteApiTarget` from the standing server's state file). `analytics-store.ts` keeps its stale-while-revalidate cache and its day slicing, now as async requests, so neither the aggregator's loop nor the server's is held for long. The `tokensCombined` field keeps the old `SUM(a+b+c+d)` arithmetic, so hourly, daily and day-of-week token totals match. Still on opencode.db: the session and tool activity counts (`session_v2`, `session_message`). No server read API covers those yet; that is recorded on #2795. Parity on live data is not shown here: it needs the laptop's populated ledger and a server running #2831. The test pins the contract with a stand-in rollup server: coverage, 7-day totals, cost rows, credential coverage, hourly and day-of-week sums, credential-key pool attribution, and that no request names a credential id. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_ --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: C3 health hooks: wire opencode-working into lane launchers and aggregator ticks (#9571)

items.title: pm-aggregator: backfill reviewed class defaults for pre-class subscriptions (#13940)
items.body: Refs #13940 — subscription class backfill for pre-class rows (#8568 gap 1). ## The gap `classEnabled()` read a class with no stored choice as off unless it was `incident`. A subscription's stored `classes` map carries only the classes of its day (creation fills the then-current defaults via `mergeClasses`; upserts touch only the keys the caller sent, #7193), so any class added after creation — `needs-drew`, `quota-wall`, `stack-health`, and the rest of the #8568 set — read OFF forever for pre-class rows, including the 2026-11-01 subscription. The preferences page already rendered those classes at their reviewed defaults, so the page said ON while the engine said OFF. ## The change `classEnabled` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/alerts.ts`): a stored choice always wins, including an explicit opt-out; a class with no stored choice takes its reviewed default from `NOTIFICATION_CLASS_DEFAULTS`; a class with no reviewed default stays off. That is the automatic backfill — it takes effect for existing rows on deploy, with no migration and no re-subscribe. New-row behavior is unchanged (`mergeClasses` at creation), and the fallback can only ever fire for classes newer than the row. Also: the `prompt-notify.ts` header comment described the old rule and is updated; the PM book tutorial `pm-stack/book/tutorials/trace-a-push.md` stated the old rule verbatim ("Legacy rows default only `incident` on") and is updated in the same change. ## Tests - Failing-first: the new regression test in `test/alerts.test.ts` — a pre-class-shaped row (`{ incident: true }`) ends with needs-drew + quota-wall + stack-health ON without re-subscribing; explicit opt-outs still read off; an unknown class stays off — failed against the old code (targeted run: 78 pass / 1 fail) and passes with the fix. The `prompt-notify` fan-out fixture now expresses its not-eligible row as an explicit opt-out, since a pre-class row is eligible under the backfill. - Targeted: `bun test test/alerts.test.ts src/prompt-notify.test.ts test/notification-preferences-3318.test.ts` — the three key tests (backfill regression, prompt fan-out, saved-toggle-is-next-engine-decision) all pass post-fix, including inside the full run. - Full suite: `bun test` in `pm-stack/aggregator` — 3353 pass / 22 fail / 2 errors, 3375 tests across 293 files. Every named failure was reproduced identically on a pristine `origin/main` control worktree in the same environment (board-cache-5082 ×5, source-gate-1195 ×1, collect-fleet-feed-args-3509 ×2: server-booting tests colliding with the live aggregator's ports, and collector subprocess tests exceeding their 60 s budget while the host runs a Nix garbage collection). None touches the alerts engine. - Typecheck: `bunx tsc --noEmit` — no errors in the touched files. Test route note: the suite ran with bun in the laptop worktree — a fleet Actions exec session cannot clone this repo (no cross-repo credentials in the runner), and this repo's CI runs on main only, so the laptop run plus the pristine-main control is the verification of record. ```json { "direct_parent": null, "links": [], "lineage": { "design": null, "roadmap_item": null, "priority": null }, "pm_meta": 1, "provenance": { "queue_id": null, "scheduled_start": null, "picked_up_at": null, "work_started_at": null, "created_at": "2026-11-24T13:44:46Z", "session_id": null, "lane": null, "host": "amd", "worktree": "/home/user/wt-lane-23266-backfill", "model": null, "lane_start_issues": [], "workspace_ref": { "kind": "worktree", "id": "/home/user/wt-lane-23266-backfill", "repo": "developing-today/code", "branch": "fix/13940-class-backfill", "sha": "81470cabcd261ca3ea40095be91039546131feb5" }, "auth_subject": "oc-code-03", "stamped_by": "fleet 0.1.0 (native)" } } ``` --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: feat(pm-stack): project page description + latest status derived from roadmap and doc/ status records (#1108)
items.body: Closes #1108 (the remaining element only; Slice 1 landed in PR #2373 and the visualization split in PR #2831). ## What The per-project page (`/program/`, pm-stack/aggregator) now renders the project's **description** and **latest status** from their sources instead of the project registry's hand-maintained copies: - **Description** — the prose paragraphs of the project's roadmap file (`planning/roadmaps/.md` in developing-today/code), read from the aggregator host's code checkout at request time. The lab-cluster registry intro duplicated this text and could drift from it. - **Latest status** — the newest `doc/_status_/` record for the project, selected by the record's own timestamp (the directory name's prefix, dash-separated time — parsed and range-validated, never file mtime), rendered with the record's own first heading and a blob link to its markdown. ## How - New `src/project-doc.ts`: pure parsers (`roadmapDescription`, `parseStatusRecordName`, `selectLatestStatusRecord`, `statusRecordTitle`, `buildProjectDocSnapshot`) plus `loadProjectDoc`, a never-throwing checkout reader in the repo-roadmap / phase-mapping discipline. - `Source.projectDoc?` optional snapshot (same pattern as `phaseMapping?`); the live source caches per slug for 5 minutes, fail-soft to the last good snapshot. - `projectDocTarget(config)` derives the target from the config's home doc — only `planning/roadmaps/*.md` home docs in the code repo qualify; `buildProjectDetail` carries the snapshot into both the HTML page and the `/api/program-project.json` twin. - Render is derived-first: when a snapshot exists it wins outright, including its absences — no prose in the roadmap renders "No prose description found…", no status record renders "No status record under doc/ for this project yet", and the hand-pinned statusReport never renders alongside a derived snapshot. When the source cannot read the checkout at all (no snapshot), the page falls back to the registry intro / statusReport exactly as before. ## Tests - New `test/project-doc.test.ts` (15 tests): description extraction (tables/lists excluded, "Latest status:" pointer cut as metadata), status-name parsing (only the `_status_` shape, invalid timestamps rejected), newest-record selection per slug, blob vs tree URLs, `loadProjectDoc` against a temp checkout (seed record rebuilt; unreadable checkout → null; missing roadmap with readable doc/ → verified absence), `projectDocTarget` qualification, and render integration (derived text renders instead of the registry copies; explicit absences render instead of the hand pin). - Hand-check against the real record (the packet's check): `loadProjectDoc` on this checkout returns the basement-cluster description from the roadmap's own prose and latest status `2026-10-27T03-14-08Z` titled "Basement cluster status, 2026-10-26" — matching `doc/2026-10-27T03-14-08Z_status_basement-cluster/`. - Affected suites: `bun test` on project-doc + program + epic-graph + phase-mapping + program-prime-5082 + projects = 116 pass / 0 fail; `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; biome format clean on all changed files (organizeImports warnings on the touched files are pre-existing on main). - Full suite: 2503 pass / 43 fail in the worktree vs 2602 pass / 32 fail on clean main the same hour — the failing sets are disjoint, environment-dependent boot/hook-timeout and feed tests (the worktree initially lacked node_modules, which alone explained the program-path boot failure: after `bun install` it passes 3/3, as does main). No test that passes on main fails because of this change in isolation. Queue task 19427 (lane any-m). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(aggregator): /frag/board honors ?done=all (#7937)
items.body: Fixes #7937 ## What PR #3855 wired `?done=all` only into the full-page `/board` route, so the board's own live-refresh fragment silently reverted a show-all Done view to the 100-card cap. Following the #8521 pattern for saved views: - `server.ts` — the `/frag/board` handler now passes `{ showAllDone: url.searchParams.get("done") === "all" }` to `renderBoardBody`, exactly like `/board`. - `board-view.ts` — `viewParamsQuery` also carries the `done` param, so `fragBoardUrl`'s refresh URLs (`data-on-load` / `data-on-dashrefresh__window`) preserve `done=all` across refresh cycles instead of dropping it. - Default behaviour is unchanged: with no `done` parameter, `/board` and `/frag/board` still render at most 100 done cards with the "show all N" link. ## Tests `bun test test/board-view-8521.test.ts` on the laptop: all 9 tests pass, including: - updated #8521 expectations (done is now carried as view state, not dropped; unrelated params like `full=1` still are); - new: `fragBoardUrl(?done=all)` → `/frag/board?done=all`; - new handler-wiring pin: the fragment handler renders show-all Done under `?done=all`. `test/author-picker-1179.test.ts` (the suite the issue suggested) fails identically on pristine main in this environment — its beforeAll spawns a server subprocess that times out (5s hook) before any test runs; pre-existing and unrelated to this diff (verified by running it in the clean primary clone). Queue task 14554, lane any-b. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: fix(pm-stack): health snapshot, incremental reconcile streams, single-flight, cached attention (#9850)
items.body: Refs #9850 — round 2. The round-1 fix (PR #10084) isolated the /health client and batched the writes, but the stalls came back: the projector was marked down twice more on the new build (2026-11-15 01:49Z and 02:55Z, ~3 min each), and /api/attention.json timed out four times in a row at the 03:00 CT reconcile fire on 2026-11-15 (35 s client timeouts, load 14→26) after flapping three times on 2026-11-14. This PR removes the mechanisms instead of widening the margins. The sentinel is unchanged — it was correctly reporting real stalls. ## Root cause 1. The reconcile `reviews` stream ignored its cursor. Every pass re-read the full PR list and made one GitHub call per PR — for developing-today/code that is 4,758 PRs — then upserted every review found: the journal shows `reviews: written=5433 ms=1692265` (28 minutes of sustained writes) and whole passes of ~11.5k rows taking 22–35 minutes, recurring roughly hourly. The `prs` stream likewise re-upserted all ~4,757 PRs every pass. 2. /health still did live DB work on the request path (a COUNT over three tables, 5 s timeout → 503). Any contention past 5 s — the mega-pass write flood above, on a loaded box — became a sentinel "down" even though the process never died. 3. POST /reconcile had no single-flight: the timer fires every ~15 min regardless, so passes overlapped and multiplied the load. 4. The aggregator's /api/attention.json re-assembled the whole view on every request (no caching), so under CPU load each request cost seconds — measured live 2026-11-15: avg 0.98 s, worst completed 24.8 s, four consecutive 35 s timeouts at the 03:00 CT reconcile fire. It was the one assembly not behind the codebase's TodayCache. ## Fix - Projector /health serves a background-refreshed snapshot (15 s refresh): zero DB work on the request path. A snapshot older than 120 s answers 503 `health_snapshot_stale` — a genuinely wedged event loop cannot refresh, so real death still reads as down; a dead process cannot answer at all. Without a snapshot provider (tests, embedders) the previous bounded live probe runs unchanged. - Reviews stream is incremental: candidates are PRs updated inside the cursor window (cursor − 5 min overlap), the PR list walk is newest-first and stops at the window edge, and a fetched PR still returns its full review list, so nothing is skipped permanently. Cursor semantics unchanged (max submitted_at; advances even when a PR errors — the #2745 contract). Measured on the live projection: 4,758 seated PRs vs 15 updated in the last 20 minutes — a pass now fetches tens of PRs instead of thousands. - prs stream: same newest-first early stop; rows at or below the cursor are not re-upserted (safe: the cursor only covers PRs an earlier unfiltered pass already upserted from pulls data); the cursor still advances over the full walk. - POST /reconcile is single-flight in serve(): a trigger during a running pass returns 200 `{ok: true, skipped: "reconcile_in_progress"}`. - Aggregator: attentionContext is wrapped in the existing TodayCache idiom (#5082) — 10 s TTL, coalesced loads, stale-while-revalidate — one cache per census variant, invalidated on the same freshness notices as the today/overview caches. ## Evidence - New regression tests: reviews-stream incremental sweep (seeded cursor → only the updated PR is fetched), prs no-re-upsert below cursor, /health serves the snapshot with a wedged DB, stale snapshot → 503, reconcile gate no-op. - Projector suite: 142 pass, 0 fail. Aggregator attention suites pass. Note: aggregator `test/today-cache-1179.test.ts` currently fails its 5 s hook timeout on pristine main as well under this box's load (verified both trees back to back) — pre-existing, unrelated to this change; the cache primitive itself is untouched. - Live A/B on a copy of the production DB (old code vs this branch): unloaded /health 4.3 ms (old, live query) vs 0.9 ms (new, snapshot, `snapshotAgeMs` present). A local write flood does not reproduce the production stall physics (production writes queue on a remote libSQL service; a local WAL file answers readers instantly), so the request-path invariant is proven by the wedged-DB test instead: /health answers 200 from the snapshot while its DB client throws on every call. - Production sampler (1 Hz, 502 samples, 2026-11-15 02:50–03:18 CT): /health max 299 ms, zero non-200; /api/attention.json avg 982 ms, worst completed 24.8 s, 4 timeouts of 35 s at 03:00–03:02 CT while load rose 13.9 → 26.1 — the flap this PR's cache removes. Deploy note: takes effect at the next switch after merge (server code is read at start). The soak gate on #9850 (gate-code-9850-soak) should restart from this deploy. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(pm): dual-ingestion slice 1 — shared Metadata check + interval sweeper (#9076)
items.body: Slice 1 of task 20270 (issue #9076, design §16 item 12): dual-ingestion interval sweeper + the shared Metadata check the webhook listener (slice 2) will reuse. ## What - `pm-stack/aggregator/src/metadata-ingestion.ts`: one `runMetadataCheck` implementation (current / generated / needs-triage), block extract/render/upsert, slug + native-parent ascertainment, `buildTriagePacket`, `storeOutcome`. - `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/metadata-sweeper.ts`: interval sweeper with strict argv contract, `--dry-run` / `--write-back` / `--forward-triage` / `--only`, lazy native-parent retry, per-repo epic-slug map (one query per run). - `pm-stack/aggregator/test/metadata-ingestion.test.ts`: 11 tests incl. a repo-task/v1 required-fields pin on the forward packet. - Follow-up fix: triage dedupe keys anchor to `issue:` per broker design (broker rejects `pr:` in triage keys). ## Live demos (real items) - Dry-run scan: `--limit 1 --dry-run` exit 0, valid summary JSON. - Test issue #13114 (created via plain gh, attached as sub-issue of #9076): live `--write-back` generated + wrote back the canonical block (direct_parent sub-issue #9076), 1 DB row stored. Block verified on the body; probe issue closed after demo. - Merged PR #13110 (no block, parentless): retroactive scan -> needs-triage -> valid packet -> triage task 21305 queued (predecessor 21300 completed by the pilot). ## Checks - `bun test test/metadata-ingestion.test.ts test/metadata-store.test.ts`: 16 pass, 0 fail. - `bunx tsc --noEmit`: clean (src + test; scripts/ excluded by tsconfig, runtime-verified via --help and 5 live runs). Closes #9076 slice 1 only. Slice 2 (webhook listener) follows separately; task 20270 stays parked with next=slice-2. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added a metadata sweep for issues and pull requests across selected repositories, with options to target specific items or run a dry run. * Added automatic metadata checks for supported GitHub issue and pull-request events. Valid metadata can be recorded and written back to the item; unresolved or conflicting parent information is flagged for triage. * Missing or invalid metadata can be rebuilt from available parent and item details. * Sweep results can be saved for future use, and items needing triage can be forwarded for review.
